newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end weaker, though undertone firm.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end weaker, though undertone firm.

text.p: Chilean shares closed slightly softer in thin trade, but the underlying tone remained optimistic with investors hoping the Central Bank will lower interest rates next month, said dealers.
Cheer over the possible rate cut is seen propelling stocks higher at the opening Thursday, they said.
"People are looking at a rates cut within the next two-three weeks at most," said one trader.
The 40-share index ended down 0.03 percent at 113.38 points. The general index shed 0.06 percent at 5,260.77 points amid turnover of 10 billion pesos.
Traders reported selective buying from institutional investors and renewed demand by foreign players for Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts.
Chilean investors reacted positively to forecasts predicting inflation will fall to 0.3 percent in March from 0.7 percent a year ago.
The market is hoping that the slowdown in inflation and recent good economic growth figures will prompt the Central Bank to lower rates, said dealers.

Losers included power utility Chilgener, whose stock is adjusting to the placement price of 2,567 pesos per share for the company's forthcoming capital increase, they said. Chilgener ended off 1.5 percent at 2,635 pesos.
Banco Edwards retreated on news merger talks with Banco de Chile have failed. Rumours of a deal had driven Edwards' stock higher in recent weeks.
Edwards A shares closed off 2.28 percent at 51 pesos.
Winners included copper products maker Madeco, up 1.99 percent at 1,025 pesos, and pulp producer Copec, which firmed 1.3 percent to 1,560 pesos.
